While the story is very well-crafted, atmospheric, and offers a poignant slice-of-life glimpse into a specific rural setting (operating a cable ferry on the Elbe), its central themes are very familiar rather than unique or original. The narrative relies on classic, well-established literary tropes: a stoic widow holding onto her late husband's traditional way of life, the contrast between rural blue-collar reality and urban corporate pressure (represented by her son/relative in Munich), and the struggle to keep a financially failing family business afloat. An average reader will appreciate the mood and character study, but they will not walk away with a "unique and original idea" that they haven't encountered in many other stories or films before.
